The joys of having the piano in the living room. As a child, I spent hours poring over the sheet music my grandmother had left for me after she passed away. Her favorite pieces, worn and dog-eared, were nestled between the couch cushions, waiting to be rediscovered. My fingers would tremble as I placed them on the keys, feeling the familiar curves of the piano's neck.

Chopin's Nocturnes were my escape. I'd lose myself in the swirling arpeggios and melancholic melodies, imagining a world beyond the walls of our small townhouse. The piano was my confidant, keeping my secrets as I practiced in the evenings, the sounds drifting up to the bedroom windows, where my siblings would disturb me, demanding their favorite tunes.

It was during those early evenings that my love for music took root. My grandmother's legacy lived on through me, as I'd experiment with the piano's dusty keys, coaxing forth new sounds that, to my untrained ears, were reminiscent of hers. Impromptu concerts would erupt on special occasions, guests coaxed into the parlor for an impromptu recital, complete with requested show-stoppers and heartfelt encores.

Years have passed, but my love for the piano remains. When the pace of life demands a spring in my step, a long-forgotten accomplishment resurfaces, a Mozart concerto that still rouses my fingers to touch the keys, a lifelong conversation restarting anew with my grandmother's musical legacy.
